prerequisites: Programming related courses (Programming Methodology, Programming Technologies and Paradigms)
Computer architecture and operating systems courses (Computer Architecture, Operating Systems)

learning_outcomes.text: Apply redundancy in systems and installations.
Know the operational metrics of a system.
Measure and model the capacity and performance of a system.
Measure and model the reliability, availability, reparability, and security of a system.
Configure systems verifying multiple operating requirements.
Assess the cost of capacity, redundancy, and security when configuring systems.
Document the technical-economic specifications of an installation in a tender document.
Specify and apply service level agreements.

syllabus_topics: 1. Introduction: System evaluation methodology, selection of techniques and metrics
2. Performance measurement: Workloads, Monitors, Visualization, Instrumentation
3. Performance evaluation: Comparison of alternatives, Empirical models
4. Performance modeling: Analytical modeling and Simulation
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the practical part (NPrac) accounts for 40% of the final grade, and the final evaluation test (NExa) accounts for 60%. All four practice reports must be submitted on time, and a minimum of 80% attendance in practical hours is required. A minimum of 50% must be obtained in NPrac to pass the practical block, and a minimum of 50% in NExa to pass the final evaluation test. If both parts are passed, the final grade is calculated as: Note = NExa * 0.6 + NPrac * 0.4. If the practical part is not passed or if the final exam is not passed (even with a passed practical part), the grade is the obtained NExa. For extraordinary calls and differentiated evaluation, the same criteria apply; students who did not pass the practical part in the ordinary call must submit all four practice reports at least one week before the extraordinary exam date, and achieve at least 50% in NPrac.
